title: Accounts Assistant
description:
- Accounts Assistant - Part Time
- Location: Eastbourne
- Hours: 12 hours per week - Tuesdays and Fridays (Flexible for the right candidate)
- Salary: £31,000 pro rata
- Job Type: Permanent

About the role

HRGO Recruitment are looking for an experienced Accounts Assistant to join our client, a leading UK-based online auction company with an innovative and fast-paced approach to its work.

This is a great opportunity for someone with previous accounts and credit control experience who enjoys variety, takes ownership of their work and is confident working independently.

Working just two days a week, you'll play an important role in keeping the day-to-day finance function running smoothly, supporting everything from invoicing and payments to credit control and supplier management.

What you'll be doing

Your responsibilities will include:
- Reconciling and processing purchase invoices, receipts, merchant payments and direct debits
- Processing weekly sales invoices
- Managing credit control, including contacting clients by phone and email
- Managing the accounts and suppliers' inboxes
- Creating weekly payment runs
- Supporting customer onboarding and offboarding
- Processing monthly supplier invoicing
- Assisting with payroll and pension queries
- Carrying out quarterly audits of management accounts, standing orders, purchase invoices and nominal codes
- Providing general support across the accounts function as required

About you

We're looking for someone who:
- Has previous experience in an accounts or finance role
- Has experience in credit control
- Is confident working independently and managing their own workload
- Is organised, accurate and comfortable working to deadlines
- Has a good eye for detail and takes pride in getting things right
- Is confident communicating with customers, suppliers and colleagues
- Has experience using accounting software - ideally Xero, Sage and Zendesk

Benefits
- 28 days holiday (Pro rata for part time roles)
- Convenient town centre office with excellent access to train links
- Active and inclusive social committee
- On-site games room stocked with complimentary snacks and drinks
- Relaxed, casual dress code
- Supportive and welcoming team environment
- Bright, modern, and open-plan workspaces

If you are interested in this exciting opportunity, please click 'APPLY NOW' and a consultant from our Eastbourne team will be in contact.

title: Legal Assistant
description:
Float Legal Secretary

Eastbourne Full-time Competitive salary + benefits

An exciting opportunity to join an established regional law firm in Eastbourne.

Are you an organised, proactive and adaptable Legal Secretary who enjoys variety in your day-to-day role? Do you thrive in a busy professional environment and enjoy working with different people and teams?

Our client, a well-regarded regional law firm based in Eastbourne, is looking to recruit a Float Legal Secretary to provide essential secretarial and administrative support across multiple departments within the firm.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys a varied workload, can confidently adapt to changing priorities and takes pride in delivering a high standard of support within a professional legal environment.

The Role

Working across a number of legal teams, you will play an important role in ensuring the smooth running of the firm's day-to-day operations. Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing high-quality secretarial and administrative support across various legal departments.
- Preparing, formatting and amending correspondence, legal documents and reports.
- Managing diaries, arranging appointments and coordinating meetings.
- Handling incoming telephone calls and correspondence in a professional and efficient manner.
- Maintaining accurate electronic and paper-based filing systems.
- Supporting fee earners and wider teams with general administrative duties and ad hoc requirements.
- Adapting to the changing needs of different departments and providing flexible cover where required.

About You

We are keen to hear from candidates who can demonstrate:
- Previous experience in a secretarial or administrative role, ideally within a legal or professional services environment.
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.
- A proactive, flexible and team-focused approach.
- A high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- The ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary and benefits package.
- The opportunity to work within an established regional law firm.
- Exposure to a variety of legal departments and practice areas.
- A supportive, friendly and collaborative working environment.
- Opportunities for professional development and career progression.
- Workplace pension scheme.

Interested?

If you are an enthusiastic and adaptable Legal Secretary looking for a varied role within a respected regional law firm, we would love to hear from you.

Apply today by submitting your CV for immediate consideration.

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
As a Payroll Assistant in Eastbourne, you will manage the day-to-day payroll administration for a growing business, helping colleagues receive accurate and timely pay. You will work within the Accounting & Finance department and keep payroll records organised for smooth monthly processes.

Client Details

The organisation operates in a well established field and is based in Eastbourne.

Description
- Process payroll information accurately and ensure records are ready for each pay run.
- Maintain employee payroll records, updating changes to pay, hours and personal details.
- Check payroll data for accuracy and resolve discrepancies before processing.
- Respond to payroll queries from employees in a clear and timely manner.
- Work with the Accounting & Finance department to provide payroll information when needed.
- Prepare payroll reports and supporting documents for internal use.
- Keep payroll files organised and handle information with appropriate confidentiality.

Profile

A successful Payroll Assistant should have:
- Experience in payroll administration and maintaining accurate payroll records.
- Confidence checking pay data and resolving discrepancies carefully.
- Ability to manage routine payroll tasks and meet regular deadlines.
- Good attention to detail when handling employee and pay information.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills for responding to payroll queries.
- Ability to work effectively with colleagues in an Accounting & Finance setting.

Job Offer
- Permanent Payroll Assistant position in Eastbourne.
- Salary of 30,000 to 34,000 dependent on the level of experience.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

title: Private Client Legal Secretary
description:
Private Client Legal Secretary - Eastbourne, East Sussex

Join a highly regarded local law firm with an excellent reputation, a welcoming culture and lovely offices.

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Private Client Legal Secretary to join a well-established law firm based in Eastbourne.

Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience

The Role:

Working closely with one fee earner, you will provide comprehensive secretarial and administrative support across all aspects of Private Client work, including wills, probate, estate administration and Lasting Powers of Attorney.

This is a varied position suited to someone who enjoys working in a client-focused legal environment, takes pride in producing accurate work and can confidently manage competing priorities. You will play an important role in supporting the day-to-day running of the department and ensuring clients receive a professional and efficient service.

Key Responsibilities:
- Providing full secretarial and administrative support to a fee earner within the Private Client team.
- Audio and copy typing legal documents, correspondence, attendance notes and file notes.
- Preparing and amending Wills, Lasting Powers of Attorney, Codicils and Probate applications.
- Assisting with estate accounts, inheritance tax forms and estate administration.
- Managing diaries, arranging appointments, meetings and client calls.
- Liaising professionally with clients, beneficiaries, executors, attorneys, financial institutions and other third parties.
- Handling incoming telephone calls and general Private Client enquiries.
- Opening new client files and completing client onboarding, identification and anti-money laundering checks.
- Managing emails, post, filing and document management.
- Supporting billing, file management and matter progression.
- Ensuring files remain accurate, up to date and compliant with internal procedures and regulatory requirements.
- Undertaking general secretarial and administrative duties to support the smooth running of the department.

About You:

To be considered for this opportunity, you will ideally have:
- Previous experience as a Legal Secretary within a Private Client department.
- A sound understanding of wills, probate and estate administration.
- Strong audio and copy typing skills, with excellent attention to detail.
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage a varied workload.
- A professional, approachable manner and confidence communicating with clients.
- Good IT skills and technical competence.

Experience with digital dictation, BigHand, Oyez Forms, Excel and Partner 4 Windows would be advantageous.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
- An established firm with a strong local reputation.
- A friendly and welcoming working culture.
- Lovely office surroundings.
- The opportunity to work closely with one fee earner in a supportive environment.
- A varied role covering a broad range of Private Client matters.
- A competitive salary based on your experience.

Apply Now:

If you are an experienced Private Client Legal Secretary looking for your next opportunity in Eastbourne, we would love to hear from you.

For immediate consideration, please submit your CV through Indeed today for a confidential discussion with Morgan Webb.

title: Administrator / Receptionist
company: South Downs Health and Care Ltd (SDHC)
advertiser_name: South Downs Health and Care Ltd (SDHC)
description: Please note that interviews will take place on 9 December. As a not-for-profit GP Federation, South Downs Health and Care is slightly different in that we are not a GP Practice with our own list of patients. Instead, we provide services at scale such as out of hours NHS GP services on behalf of local practices (pre-booked appointments), Covid Vaccination Services and much more! SDHC also provide a Private GP service to the local community. We have an exciting opportunity for two Administrators/Receptionists to join our busy, friendly and supportive team on a permanent, full-time basis. You will join our team of GPs, GP Trainees, Advanced Clinical Practitioners, Vaccinators and Phlebotomists who work extremely hard in providing services to support GP Practices in East Sussex. Working as part of a team this role involves: provision of administrative support for all SDHC clinical services, to ensure professional operational standards and excellence in patient care and safety are maintained; face-to-face reception to provide shift cover and other back office administrative functions as required to meet the needs of the business including services provided to our member GP practices. Critical to the success of the services will be the need to engage and work with practices and clinicians to ensure agreed service levels are met. The role may sometimes require travel to other sites in East Sussex including sometimes at short notice to resolve operational or staffing problems. SDHC operational hours are 08:00 22:30 seven days a week for which a rota is in place. Daily monitoring of the email inboxes, follow up any issues raised by patients or staff and highlighting any concerns appropriately Support patient and staff queries; and the services complaints and incidents procedures Cover the reception desk when required during shift times and present a professional and courteous image to all service users, visitors and staff Welcome visitors and provide all possible assistance, including arrangements for access requirements, ensuring that the appropriate staff member is informed of their arrival Assist with training and site inductions for all new staff as required Undertake crosschecks across the service to ensure patient safety and service quality is being maintained as per protocols Support the smooth and safe operation of company site(s) including stock checking Undertake other service-related duties, such as support with booking, cancelling or rescheduling of clinics, referrals and, as required, support with practice tasks and other duties that avoids any additional workload passing back to practices from the service. Communicate courteously and politely at all times when dealing with enquiries Use of computer and some paper-based systems to perform administrative functions, in order to support the administration of service provision in accordance with agreed standard processes and procedures, within agreed timeframes. Ensure the accuracy and quality of data recorded Provide administration support to senior team members as required. This may involve a mixture of regular and ad hoc tasks. Other Duties Co-ordinate, attend and/or facilitate meetings, and if required, transcribe any minutes and notes Other project related assistance as required by the organisation. This may include providing cross cover to supporting other services that SDHC delivers or may deliver including, but not limited to, clinical correspondence, pathology and clinical teams. This job description is not exhaustive. SDHC reserves the right to require you to undertake any other duties and to support colleagues across all areas of the company at the request of the line manager and it is a condition of your employment that you are prepared to do this. Personal Contribution We want to create an environment where everyone finds it easy to both do the work and improve the work. For this to be successful you will: Maintain productive relationships encouraging the giving and receiving of regular feedback to create and maintain a culture of constantly seeking to refine and improve the service and learn together Be responsible for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Be responsible for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Work collaboratively to help develop and promote a positive working culture, including involvement in developing, improving and promoting the service Ensure adherence to efficient administrative processes within the services Support services to attain high standards for access, quality, safety and patient engagement achieved through organisationally agreed objectives and goals Quality Alert the Services Lead to any issues compromising the quality of services, projects and operational workstreams Work within the relevant risk management and health and safety policies and procedures Adhere to a robust process for recording learning events, complaints, accidents and significant events Provide administrative support to assist with the development and management of any changes or new processes and systems that need implementing Carry out any other appropriate duties as determined by the organisation Communication Provide professional telephone and written support to patients and their carers Respond to queries from patients and staff in a professional manner referring to the appropriate colleagues in accordance with protocols and professional boundaries. Accountable and responsible for own actions, working within professional boundaries and competencies. Contribute to the continual improvement of the administrative service, sharing best practice and speaking up when things go wrong Provide support within your team (including but not limited to participation in buddying/ mentoring of new colleagues, raising tensions in respectful and courteous manners, attendance and contribution to team meetings and discussions) Support team members to deliver excellent service through a programme of peer review and direct observation of practice. Patient & Public Involvement Support the company's aim to optimise patient wellbeing Engage with patients, internal and external stakeholders as required Engage with users of the service to understand peoples experience of the service and to measure levels of satisfaction Contribute to ensuring the patient voice is heard and acted on appropriately. Particular attention will be paid to how we ensure the care we provide is safe, effective, caring, and responsive. Contribute to responding to complaints when requested as appropriate, according to the SDHC complaints policy. Risk Management Engage in a culture where the sharing of learning events and deep learning that comes from them is positive and the norm. Contribute to a learning event register which is maintained and where required actions are completed within agreed timescales Undertake risk assessments if required, in which case training will be given Audit Participate in audit activities to optimise patient safety and the use of resource, undertaking audits in accordance with the service audit plan to evidence SDHCs ability to provide Safe, Effective, Caring, Responsive, and Well-Led services Contribute to recommendations based on the outcomes of audit and shared learning activities Information and IT Data that helps us understand services, practices and patients is important to SDHC. You will help ensure we capture and analyse important data that helps drive continuous service improvement Support service audit as required Support the development and utilise agreed searches and templates to ensure high quality consistent patient care and enable data collection and reporting on activity Use various IT systems including Microsoft Office Collaborative Support Work within a team who provide peer support to each other Travel between locations across the patch if and when required Work alongside other SDHC teams as required to ensure seamless patient care If you like being busy and enjoy working within an administrative role in a supportive environment with friendly teams, this role is for you. Key working relationships SDHC service leads Senior Leadership Team Other public sector organisations Third sector organisations Hillbrow Health and Wellbeing staff

title: Admin Assistant
description: To provide a comprehensive and efficient administration support to the team including handling correspondence and dealing with telephone enquiries. Liaison with other directorates, agencies and staff at all levels both internally and externally. Ensure that all documents and correspondence are dealt with correctly being uploaded into the electronic patient record system. Recording attendance at out-patient appointments by service users on the electronic patient record system. To be responsible for processing and sending out-patient appointment letters once typed and approved with a variety of self-help information when advised to do so. Open and process incoming and outgoing mail (including emails) for the team. Ensure all information is handled in a confidential manner in line with relevant policies. Organisation of non-urgent patient transport for service users when requested Photocopying, faxing and filing as required. Maintaining stationery supplies and requesting items to be ordered timely by supervisors. Provision of cover for other members of the administration team. Any other administrative tasks appropriate for the grade. Assist with all administrative tasks required for the role, including monitoring the admin inbox, covering colleagues breaks, covering reception and telephones. Assisting clinical colleagues with administrative tasks Secretarial duties: Assisting with appointment letters/discharge letters, Taking minutes for MDT and professional meetings. Reception duties: Provide reception duties, meet and greet visitors and patients, taking accurate messages and providing follow up actions. Telephone duties: on rotation answering incoming calls to St Mary's House, taking accurate messages and actioning and requests.

title: Patient Services Administrator
description: Due to expansion of our team, Park Practice GP surgery is looking to recruit a part-time Patient Services Administrator to work as part of our excellent and well-established team at Park Practice. The right person will have the skills and ability to work in a busy and demanding environment, with excellent communication and interpersonal skills. The successful applicant will be employed for 33 hours across the week (days and working hours to be confirmed subject to business need). Hours to be covered are 8am to 6.30pm. We also open 6.00pm-8.00pm on a Wednesday evening. The successful applicant will be expected to work this evening on a rotational basis (approximately 1 in 8). Your role as a Patient Services Administrator will require you to be the face of the practice. You will work in a very fast-paced environment, and the role will include answering the telephones, manning the reception desk, processing prescriptions, dealing with queries or carrying out administrative tasks. Key responsibilities include: Answering/forwarding incoming calls Handling and answering enquiries accurately and completely without dispensing advice, breaching patient confidentiality or making medical judgements Assit patients in completing online triage forms Dealing with patient queries Checking patients in for appointments Dealing with payments from patients Processing prescriptions and dealing with prescription queries Be aware of and abide by practice protocols and policies Verify new patient registrations Book recalls as advised by clinical staff Keep reception area clean and tidy Skills required: Strong communicator Excellent team working Organised and diligent Punctual Confident and responsible Excellent customer service skills Ability to prioritise and organise a busy day Calm and pleasant manner Resilience Starting salary for this role will be in line with national minimum wage. Please note that interviews for this position will initially take place via video call / telephone. We respectfully request that recruitment agencies do not contact us regarding this vacancy. The Patient Services Administrator is the first-line contact for most patients and other professionals, medical and allied staff. The main purpose of the job is to ensure that patients enquiries of whatever nature are dealt with efficiently and promptly, and that sufficient information is given to doctors and other staff at all times. Administrators work in a rota system covering all aspects of the practice administration system (telephone, front desk, prescriptions, Docman, results). Some post holders may also hold designated lead or specialist responsibilities in specific administrative areas, in addition to these core duties.
